chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Awwaz and Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

We asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who divorced his wife and testified to the revocatory divorce (raj'ah) but did not have sexual intercourse, then he divorced her again in another period of purity in accordance with the Sunnah. Is the second divorce established without sexual intercourse? He said: Yes, if he testified to the revocatory divorce and did not have sexual intercourse, the divorce is considered the second one.

key_terms.الرَّجْعَة: Revocatory divorce (where the husband can take back his wife without a new contract)
key_terms.السُّنَّة: The Prophetic tradition or standard legal procedure
key_terms.طُلْقَة: Divorce (specifically referring to the count of divorces)
key_terms.طُهْر: Period of purity (menstrual-free period in which divorce can be pronounced)

ai.seo_question: Does sexual intercourse count as a condition for the validity of the second divorce if the first was revocable?
ai.summary: In al-istibsar, Shaykh al-Tusi uses this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the condition of 'consummation' (muwa'qah) for the validity of the second divorce during the waiting period (iddah). This ruling is pivotal in Shia jurisprudence as it distinguishes between the revocable first divorce and the binding second, emphasizing that mere testimony without physical intimacy does not trigger the finality of the third divorce. This highlights the Shia emphasis on the literal and practical conditions of marital dissolution as derived from the Imams' interpretations.
